alt.en: A hand-coloured botanical engraving numbered 1267: an upright stem of ivy with broad, glossy, pointed oval leaves, topped by a rounded cluster of small greenish flowers and a cluster of round green berries. Behind it are uncoloured outline drawings of lobed ivy leaves, a coloured five-lobed leaf sits at lower left, and at the foot are small drawings of a flower and of a dark purple berry, whole and cut open.
alt.es: Grabado botánico coloreado a mano con el número 1267: un tallo erguido de hiedra con hojas anchas, brillantes, ovaladas y puntiagudas, rematado por un ramillete redondo de florecillas verdosas y un racimo de bayas verdes y redondas. Detrás hay dibujos sin colorear, solo de contorno, de hojas lobuladas de hiedra; abajo a la izquierda, una hoja coloreada de cinco lóbulos, y al pie, pequeños dibujos de una flor y de una baya morada oscura, entera y abierta por la mitad.

caption.en: Ivy, the holly's partner in the carol's first line, in plate 1267 of Sowerby and Smith's English Botany (London, 1804), shown in flower and in berry.
caption.es: La hiedra, compañera del acebo en el primer verso del villancico, en la lámina 1267 de English Botany de Sowerby y Smith (Londres, 1804), con flores y con bayas.

source: James Edward Smith and James Sowerby, English Botany, vol. 18 (London: printed by R. Taylor, sold by J. Sowerby, 1804), plate 1267, "Hedera Helix, Common Ivy" (plate imprint "Feby. 1. 1804. Published by Jas. Sowerby, London.")

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "VII. THE HOLLY AND THE IVY.", numbered 17 and marked "Andante moderato", with a voice line in one sharp and 3/4 time above a two-staff piano part. Under the notes run the words "The holly and the ivy, When they are both full grown, Of all the trees that are in the wood, The holly bears the crown" and the start of the refrain, "The rising of the sun".
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "VII. THE HOLLY AND THE IVY.", con el número 17 y la indicación "Andante moderato", con una línea de canto con un sostenido en la clave y en 3/4 sobre un acompañamiento de piano en dos pentagramas. Bajo las notas va la letra "The holly and the ivy, When they are both full grown, Of all the trees that are in the wood, The holly bears the crown" y el comienzo del estribillo, "The rising of the sun".

caption.en: The Holly and the Ivy as No. VII of Cecil Sharp's English Folk-Carols (London, 1911), page 17: Mary Clayton's tune in G and 3/4 with Sharp's piano part, the printing our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: The Holly and the Ivy como n.º VII de English Folk-Carols de Cecil Sharp (Londres, 1911), página 17: la melodía de Mary Clayton en Sol y en 3/4 con el acompañamiento de piano de Sharp, la edición de la que parte nuestro arreglo.

source: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Carols, with Pianoforte Accompaniment and an Introduction and Notes (London: Novello, 1911), No. VII, p. 17, "The Holly and the Ivy"

alt.en: A hand-coloured botanical engraving numbered 496: an upright sprig of holly with dark green, wavy, spiny leaves and a cluster of small white flowers where the leaves meet the stem. At the foot are small drawings of a single white flower, a red berry cut open and two seeds.
alt.es: Grabado botánico coloreado a mano con el número 496: una ramita erguida de acebo con hojas verde oscuro, onduladas y espinosas, y un ramillete de florecillas blancas donde las hojas se unen al tallo. Al pie hay pequeños dibujos de una flor blanca suelta, una baya roja abierta y dos semillas.

caption.en: Holly in flower, plate 496 of Sowerby and Smith's English Botany (London, 1798), whose text says it flowers in May and is used "to ornament churches and houses at Christmas".
caption.es: Acebo en flor, lámina 496 de English Botany de Sowerby y Smith (Londres, 1798), cuyo texto dice que florece en mayo y que se usa "to ornament churches and houses at Christmas", para adornar iglesias y casas en Navidad.

source: James Edward Smith and James Sowerby, English Botany, vol. 7 (London: printed by J. Davis, sold by J. Sowerby, 1798), plate 496, "Ilex Aquifolium, Common Holly"
